verdicts.reason: Both lose the coffee bag entirely. The photo becomes a blurry brown block, and the product survives only as a tiny icon next to an equally tiny logo beside the CTA. The SAVE 15% pill is oversized, runs off the canvas edge and competes with the headline. A also wraps the body copy to two cramped lines, with a dead left zone before the blur. B keeps the body on one line but leaves the blur block floating with empty space on the right.

Both use the same broken parts: the blurry block instead of the bag, a micro-sized logo and bag icon, and a giant SAVE pill cut off at the canvas edge that outweighs the headline. A reads left to right with the body on one clean line. B wraps the body copy to two lines, leaving the text block cramped next to a large empty blur area on the right.

A pulls the Build a Subscription CTA away from its copy and strands it, very small, at the far left. The CTA ends up the weakest thing on the canvas, after the body text and a tiny logo and bag icon, which breaks both grouping and hierarchy. B keeps the headline, body and CTA together in one block. It still has the shared flaws: the blurry photo block, a tiny logo, and an oversized SAVE pill cut off at the right edge.

A puts a cut-off SAVE pill on the left, wraps the body to two cramped lines, and leaves a large empty blur rectangle on the right with dead space beyond it. B has a cleaner left-to-right flow: blur block, text, CTA, then badge, with the body on one line. It still loses the bag, shrinks the logo to an unreadable size, and lets the clipped, oversized SAVE pill compete with the headline.
